# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## Primary Classification Axes

The taxonomy is organized by **primary mechanic**, with secondary notes on constraint type and solution object.

---

## 1. NUMBER PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*The solver places numbers into cells according to numeric or counting constraints.*

### 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness-Based
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Sudoku** | Each number appears once per row, column, and region |
| **Ripple Effect** | Numbers in each region are 1–n; same numbers separated by distance |
| **Makaro** | Numbers fill regions; arrow cells indicate largest neighbor |

### 1.2 Count / Sum Constraints
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Nansuke** | Numbers indicate the size of connected same-number groups |
| **Kurotto** | Black circles contain numbers summing connected black-cell group sizes |
| **Nagareru** | Numbers flow along paths with directional constraints |

---

## 2. REGION / AREA DIVISION PUZZLES
*The solver divides the grid into distinct regions or shapes.*

### 2.1 Polyomino-Based Division
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Fillomino** | Divide into polyominoes; each cell contains its region's size; no two same-size regions touch |
| **Five Cells** | Divide into pentominoes following clue constraints |
| **Shikaku** | Divide into rectangles; numbered cells indicate rectangle area |
| **LITS** | Shade one tetromino per region; shaded cells connected; no 2×2 shaded blocks; same tetrominoes don't touch |
| **Double Choco** | Divide into regions each containing equal white and shaded halves of identical shape |
| **Evolomino** | Divide into polyominoes of increasing size following evolution rules |
| **Nuritwin** | Divide grid into pairs of identically shaped shaded regions |

### 2.2 Shape & Connectivity Rules
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Nurikabe** | Shade cells so white islands match numbered clues; all black cells connected; no 2×2 black blocks |
| **Heyawake** | Shade cells in rooms; no two shaded cells adjacent; unshaded cells form single connected group per row/column crossing rules |
| **Choco Banana** | Shade cells into rectangles; numbered clues indicate size of rectangle containing that cell |
| **Tilepaint** | Shade cells so each rectangular region is entirely shaded or unshaded according to clues |

### 2.3 Region + Number Hybrid
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Sto-stone** | Place stones in regions; stones fall to bottom; each region has exactly one stone |
| **Chained Block** | Numbered blocks are connected in chains with specific size constraints |

---

## 3. PATH & LOOP PUZZLES
*The solver draws a path or closed loop through the grid.*

### 3.1 Single Closed Loop
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Slitherlink** | Draw a single closed loop along grid edges; numbers indicate how many sides of that cell the loop uses |
| **Masyu** | Loop passes through all circles; white circles — straight through, turn before/after; black circles — turn on, straight before/after |
| **Yajilin** | Loop passes through non-shaded cells; arrows indicate count of shaded cells in that direction |
| **Mid-loop** | Loop passes through midpoints of edges under specific crossing/turning constraints |
| **Moon-or-Sun** | Loop alternates moon and sun regions; must pass through all symbols |
| **Dotchi-Loop** | Loop uses either all square corners or all diagonal corners in each region |
| **Nurimeizu** | Loop-based maze shading with region boundary constraints |

### 3.2 Open Paths / Trails
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Numberlink** | Connect matching numbered pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping paths that fill the entire grid |
| **Pencils** | Draw straight-line pencil strokes to fill the grid; clues indicate stroke lengths or endpoints |
| **Hebi** | Draw snakes of specified lengths through the grid without touching each other |
| **Suraromu** | Paths travel through grid cells following directional and length constraints |

### 3.3 Flow / Movement Paths
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Nagareru** | *(also listed under 1.2)* Numbers and arrows indicate flow direction through the grid |
| **Satogaeri** | Move circles back to their home regions along non-crossing paths |
| **Yosenabe** | Slide numbered tiles toward each other so matching groups sum correctly |

---

## 4. CELL STATE (SHADE / UNSHADE) PUZZLES
*The solver determines a binary state — typically black or white — for each cell.*

### 4.1 Clue-Directed Shading
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Hitori** | Shade cells so no number repeats in a row/column; shaded cells don't touch; unshaded cells connected |
| **Kurodoko** | Shade cells; white numbered cells see exactly that many white cells in a line; no two shaded cells adjacent; all white cells connected |
| **Usowan** | Numbers in rooms indicate shaded neighbor cells; exactly one number per room is a liar |
| **Norinori** | Shade exactly two cells per region; every shaded cell shares an edge with exactly one other shaded cell (forming dominoes) |
| **Nurimisaki** | Shade cells leaving white "peninsula" cells; each unshaded island has exactly one end cell |
| **Akari** | Place light bulbs to illuminate all white cells; bulbs may not illuminate each other; numbers constrain adjacent bulbs |

### 4.2 Geometric / Shape Shading
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Shakashaka** | Place right triangles in white cells so all remaining white areas form rectangles |
| **Sashigane** | Shade L-shaped (sashigane) regions; numbered cells indicate arm lengths |
| **Juosan** | Draw horizontal or vertical lines in each cell; lines of the same orientation don't connect across region boundaries |

---

## 5. OBJECT PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*The solver places discrete objects (lights, bridges, symbols) into the grid.*

### 5.1 Connection / Bridge Placement
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Hashiwokakero** | Connect numbered islands with bridges; bridge count matches island number; all islands connected; bridges don't cross |

### 5.2 Symbol / Token Placement
| Puzzle | Core Constraint |
|--------|----------------|
| **Akari** | *(also listed under 4.1)* Place light bulbs; illumination and adjacency constraints |
| **Yosenabe** | *(also listed under 3.3)* Place/move tokens so groups reach target sums |

---

## 6. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC PUZZLES
*Puzzles combining shading + paths, regions + numbers, or other compound mechanics.*

| Puzzle | Combined Mechanics |
|--------|-------------------|
| **Kurotto** | Shading + numeric region-sum clues |
| **Suraromu** | Path-drawing + directional numeric clues |
| **Chained Block** | Region division + ordered connectivity |
| **Evolomino** | Region division + sequential sizing logic |
| **Nagareru** | Flow paths + numeric constraints |
| **Nansuke** | Number placement + region grouping |

---

## Cross-Reference: Constraint Type

| Constraint Type | Puzzles |
|----------------|---------|
| **Connectivity** (all cells of a type must connect) | Nurikabe, Hitori, Kurodoko, Hashiwokakero, Heyawake |
| **No 2×2 blocks** | Nurikabe, LITS, Heyawake |
| **Counting neighbors** | Slitherlink, Akari, Usowan, Kurodoko |
| **Region sizing** | Fillomino, Shikaku, Choco Banana, Five Cells |
| **Path non-crossing** | Numberlink, Satogaeri, Hashiwokakero |
| **Loop continuity** | Slitherlink, Masyu, Yajilin, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop |
| **Symmetry / mirroring** | Double Choco, Nuritwin, Shakashaka |

---

## Summary Tree

```
Grid-Based Logic Puzzles
├── 1. Number Placement
│   ├── 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness (Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Makaro)
│   └── 1.2 Count / Sum (Nansuke, Kurotto, Nagareru)
├── 2. Region / Area Division
│   ├── 2.1 Polyomino (Fillomino, Five Cells, Shikaku, LITS, Double Choco, Evolomino, Nuritwin)
│   ├── 2.2 Shape & Connectivity (Nurikabe, Heyawake, Choco Banana, Tilepaint)
│   └── 2.3 Region + Number Hybrid (Sto-stone, Chained Block)
├── 3. Path & Loop
│   ├── 3.1 Single Closed Loop (Slitherlink, Masyu, Yajilin, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nurimeizu)
│   ├── 3.2 Open Paths (Numberlink, Pencils, Hebi, Suraromu)
│   └── 3.3 Flow / Movement (Nagareru, Satogaeri, Yosenabe)
├── 4. Cell State (Shade/Unshade)
│   ├── 4.1 Clue-Directed (Hitori, Kurodoko, Usowan, Norinori, Nurimisaki, Akari)
│   └── 4.2 Geometric Shading (Shakashaka, Sashigane, Juosan)
├── 5. Object Placement
│   ├── 5.1 Bridge Placement (Hashiwokakero)
│   └── 5.2 Symbol Placement (Akari, Yosenabe)
└── 6. Hybrid / Multi-Mechanic
    (Kurotto, Suraromu, Chained Block, Evolomino, Nagareru, Nansuke)
```

---

> **Note:** Several puzzles appear in multiple categories because their mechanics genuinely span more than one primary type. The primary listing reflects the dominant solving activity; secondary listings note meaningful crossover.
